text_blocks.snippet: To help COVID-19 go away, focus on supportive care and, if eligible, specific treatments. Supportive care includes rest, hydration, and over-the-counter medications for symptoms like fever and cough. For those at higher risk of severe illness, antiviral medications may be prescribed to prevent the virus from worsening, according to the CDC.
snippet_highlighted_words: focus on supportive care and, if eligible, specific treatments

list.snippet: Rest: Getting adequate rest allows your body's immune system to focus on fighting the virus.
Hydration: Drinking plenty of fluids, like water, helps to keep your body functioning properly and can help with symptom relief.
Symptom Management: Over-the-counter medications like fever reducers (e.g., acetaminophen or ibuprofen) and cough suppressants can help manage symptoms and improve comfort.
Certain antiviral medications can be prescribed for individuals at higher risk of severe COVID-19.
These medications work by targeting the virus and preventing it from replicating in the body.
According to the CDC, these treatments can help reduce the severity of the illness and prevent hospitalization.
To prevent the spread of the virus, it's important to isolate from others, especially if you are experiencing symptoms.
This includes staying home from work or school and avoiding close contact with people outside your household.
Individuals with weakened immune systems may need to isolate for longer periods.
If you have concerns about your symptoms or are at higher risk of complications, it's crucial to consult with a healthcare professional.
They can assess your individual situation and determine the most appropriate course of treatment.

related_questions.question: What damage can COVID do to your body?
related_questions.snippet: By some estimates, 400 million people worldwide have been diagnosed with some form of long Covid. But an infection can also lead to other issues, including lung and heart damage and microbiome changes in the gut, that may not always be recognized as long Covid but can still have a lasting effect on our health.
related_questions.title: A Clearer Picture of Covid's Lasting Effects on the Body

text_blocks.snippet: COVID-19 can lead to a range of complications, including acute respiratory distress syndrome, heart problems, and blood clots. Some individuals also experience long-term symptoms, often referred to as long COVID, which can include ongoing respiratory issues, fatigue, and neurological problems. Severe COVID-19 can also worsen existing medical conditions.
snippet_highlighted_words: acute respiratory distress syndrome, heart problems, and blood clots

list.title: Respiratory Issues:
list.snippet: Pneumonia, acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), and difficulty breathing.

list.title: Cardiovascular Problems:
list.snippet: Heart inflammation (myocarditis and pericarditis), blood clots, and potentially triggering or worsening existing heart conditions.

list.title: Other Organ Damage:
list.snippet: Kidney injury, liver damage, and neurological issues.

list.title: Inflammatory Response:
list.snippet: An overreaction of the immune system, potentially leading to systemic inflammation and organ damage.

list.title: Worsening of Underlying Conditions:
list.snippet: COVID-19 can exacerbate existing conditions like diabetes, obesity, and cardiovascular disease.
Persistent Respiratory Symptoms: Shortness of breath, cough, and reduced lung capacity.
Fatigue and Muscle Aches: Prolonged tiredness, weakness, and muscle pain.
Neurological Issues: Cognitive problems ("brain fog"), headaches, and sleep disturbances.
Cardiovascular Issues: Increased risk of heart problems even after the initial infection.
Psychological Effects: Anxiety, depression, and post-traumatic stress.

text_blocks.snippet: Risk Factors for Severe COVID-19 and Complications:

list.snippet: Age: Older adults are at higher risk for severe illness and complications.
Underlying Medical Conditions: Individuals with conditions like diabetes, obesity, heart disease, and lung disease are more vulnerable.
Obesity: Obesity is a significant risk factor for severe COVID-19.
Compromised Immune System: Individuals with weakened immune systems are more susceptible to severe illness.
